title: Will bamboo ever smell of sandalwood?
odia:
ଆଉ କି ସେଦିନ ଆସିବ
ବାଉଁସ ଗଛରେ ମଳୟ ଲାଗିଲେ
ଚନ୍ଦନ ପରାଏ ବାସିବ।
literal_meaning: Will that day ever come, when the Malaya breeze touches the bamboo and it smells like sandalwood?
meaning_odia: ମଳୟ ପବନ ଲାଗିଲେ ବାଉଁଶ ଚନ୍ଦନ ପରି ବାସିବ କି—ଏହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ବାହାରର ପ୍ରଭାବରୁ ଅସାଧାରଣ ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତନ ଆସିବାର ଆଶାକୁ ନେଇ ସନ୍ଦେହ ପ୍ରକାଶ ପାଇଛି ବୋଲି ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The imagined breeze promises a fragrance that belongs to sandalwood, while the plant remains bamboo. This edition reads the opening question as doubt that a hoped-for change will arrive merely through a favourable influence. The verse leaves the question hanging; it does not supply a named person or event.
usage_example: Someone expects a new setting alone to transform a habit they have made no effort to change. A reader might recall this question about bamboo and sandalwood. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: ମଳୟ is read as the Malaya or southern spring breeze. Here breeze and sandalwood fragrance form a poetic image of influence and transformation. The verse is not presented as a botanical claim that wind changes one plant into another, or as proof that people cannot change.
